A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. The original proofs, pre-image discussion, and benchmark results can be matched across the appendix reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original regression experiments across eleven datasets and four base models, including CRPS scores and calibration-test results in Table 1 and Figures 1–7.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds conformal-prediction comparisons, direct kernel-regression comparisons, and runtime experiments in Appendices D–G.

M1.justification: The distribution kernel, CKME coefficient calculation, and simplex projection producing weighted empirical predictions remain unchanged. New Algorithms 1–2 summarize existing steps; v1's pre-image procedure in Appendix B is retained in v2 Appendix C.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same nine UCI regression datasets, Bike Sharing, and bimodal synthetic dataset. The added interval and computational evaluations reuse this regression coverage or vary representation sample counts without introducing new data populations or input scenarios.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated comparisons against Chernozhukov et al.'s split conformal prediction in Appendix D, unrecalibrated kernelized distribution regression in Appendix F, and a naive Gaussian-type kernel implementation in Appendix E. The original PIT, GPBETA, None(T), and None(T+C) comparisons remain.

E3.justification: New protocols evaluate nominal 95% intervals using coverage, relative width, and interval–PIT distance correlation; normalize direct-kernel comparisons to that baseline's CRPS; and measure runtime. Figure 5 fixes 300 predictions while varying distribution samples from 500 to 5000. The original benchmark splits and evaluation procedures remain; the newly disclosed regularization tuning does not establish a rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix E adds an EDK efficiency ablation across representation sizes, Appendix F investigates whether direct kernel regression removes the need for separate recalibration, and Appendix G analyzes runtime against PIT. Appendix D additionally examines prediction-dependent error cancellation through distance correlation.

E5.justification: Figure 5 newly specifies at least 25 timing trials per configuration. The original benchmark's 20 repetitions and standard-deviation reporting are retained; the PDFs do not establish increased repetition of those original experiments.

E6.justification: Table 1's numerical values and all seven original plots are retained, with the detailed plots renumbered 8–11. New Figures 4–7 report interval quality, direct-kernel performance, and runtime findings. These include substantially faster EDK computation and severe naval undercoverage: roughly 25–30% for recalibrated GDN, MDN, and BNN versus approximately 95% for conformal prediction.

T1.justification: New Appendix B establishes the connection to grouping loss and adds Proposition B.1 with a proof equating expected-score minimization with entropy minimization subject to auto-calibration under realizability. Remark 5.3 newly states a compact-metric target-space requirement. The original principal results and Appendix A proofs are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, principal contributions, and conclusion retain their central claims. The introduction changes its specific claim of better calibration from comparison with Kuleshov et al.'s PIT method to Song et al.'s parametric recalibration approach.

C2.justification: New Section 7 explicitly discusses cubic calibration-set complexity, difficulties comparing complex distributions, insufficient feature-conditional calibration, and loss of continuous-density structure. Added appendix discussions explain the two-stage modeling rationale and implementation-dependent runtime. Appendix D also introduces an interpretation of comparable conformal coverage that understates the naval exceptions in Figure 4.

D1.justification: Section 6.3 newly documents five-fold regularization selection and its CKME objective. Added experiments disclose kernel/grid tuning, NVIDIA A100 hardware, and 1000-sample inverse-CDF representation for PIT timing. The code reference changes from recalibration_experiment to recalibration_icml2026. These are documentation and access-reference additions, without evidence that the original method changed.

R1.justification: Related work expands substantially to classification calibration, multicalibration, local calibration, conformal prediction, and grouping loss. Section 4 and Appendix B acknowledge quantitative equivalence with Kull and Flach's grouping loss, materially refining the positioning of the decomposition and emphasizing its information-theoretic interpretation.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main narrative order remain intact. Local editing, algorithm summaries, a dedicated limitations section, impact and acknowledgement text, and revised appendix organization improve exposition without extensive rewriting of the retained material.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a conference layout with different typography, first-page structure, and running headers, and adds two algorithm boxes and four substantive figures. Existing plots are resized or relocated. Figure 2 and Table 1 captions correct 'test set' to 'train set,' and Figure 2 gains explanatory discussion.

improvement.justification: The direct-kernel comparison and timing studies address important gaps in v1's empirical justification of the two-stage design and efficiency claims. Appendix B strengthens theoretical positioning, while tuning disclosures and explicit limitations improve reproducibility and applicability guidance. A material weakness is Appendix D's broad coverage-comparability claim despite severe naval undercoverage in Figure 4. The substantial gains in validation and transparency outweigh that overstatement.
